# Results — Study 603 (Treasury Auction Concession)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test (dealer
folklore, formalised by Lou-Yan-Zhang 2013 and Fleming-Rosenberg 2008) — **yields cheapen into
big 10Y/30Y Treasury auctions and richen after; dealers demand a concession to absorb the
supply** — measured on every 10-Year Note and 30-Year Bond auction since 1979 (TreasuryDirect /
FiscalData official records, reopenings included) against the CBOE ^TNX/^TYX daily yield tape
and TLT. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the yield tape's last session inside it is 2026-06-26).
Fingerprints `388e6555b83b` (yields) · `7d6a23aca7db` (TLT + bills).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Auctions | **825** auctions (**496** × 10Y notes, **329** × 30Y bonds), 1979-10-31 → 2026-06-11, from `api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov` `auctions_query` (the TreasuryDirect feed); reopenings included — a 9-Year-10-Month reopening is the same supply event |
| Yield tape | ^TNX / ^TYX daily closes in %, 16,108 rows, 1962-01-02 → 2026-06-26 (yfinance) — **492** 10Y and **329** 30Y auctions land on the tape with full ±5-day windows |
| Tradability tape | TLT **total-return** (auto-adjusted) closes + ^IRX 13-week bill rate, 6,018 rows, 2002-07-30 → 2026-06-30 |
| Windows | pre = the 5 trading days **ending on the auction-day close** (results hit at 1 pm ET, so that close includes the stop-out); post = the 5 trading days after |
| Primary test | daily Δy (bps) on `[1, D_pre, D_post]` with **Newey-West (HAC, 8 lags)** t — handles overlapping 10Y/30Y refunding-week windows and serial correlation; the Welch pre-vs-baseline t is supporting only (rolling baseline windows overlap) |
| Execution / costs | TLT leg: the auction calendar is public weeks ahead; enter at the **auction-day close**, first return earned is A→A+1 — exactly **one execution lag**; 2 and 5 bps **one-way × NAV per leg**; cash days earn the 13-week bill rate; all races **excess-vs-excess**; long-only, no borrow |

## The concession — yield changes around auctions (real tape)

| tenor | n auctions | pre-window (cum) | post-window (cum) | ordinary 5-day baseline | HAC t (pre) | HAC t (post) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **10Y** | 492 | **+1.55 bps** | −1.20 bps | +0.00 bps (n = 9,419) | **+2.15** | −1.99 |
| **30Y** | 329 | **+2.18 bps** | −0.62 bps | −0.49 bps (n = 7,564) | **+3.27** | −0.52 |

HAC regression detail (the primary): 10Y pre **+0.324 bps/day** (window +1.62 bps, t = **+2.15**),
post −0.283 bps/day (window −1.41 bps, t = **−1.99**), 16,107 days; 30Y pre **+0.548 bps/day**
(window +2.74 bps, t = **+3.27**), post −0.080 bps/day (window −0.40 bps, t = **−0.52**),
12,365 days. Supporting Welch pre-vs-baseline t: 10Y **+2.19**, 30Y **+3.36**.

**The cheapen-into leg is REAL on both tenors** (HAC t = 2.15 and 3.27 — a 1.5–3 bps concession
built over the auction week). **The richen-after leg is not certified in yield space**: 10Y
t = −1.99 sits just under the bar and 30Y t = −0.52 is nowhere — hence the split **MIXED**
stamp. No survivorship anywhere: the auction list is the official complete record and the yield
indices are constant-maturity, not a survivor panel.

## Era split — the concession moved eras, it didn't die

| tenor · era | pre bps/day | HAC t (pre) | post bps/day | HAC t (post) | n auctions |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10Y 1979–2007 | +0.171 | +0.53 | −0.483 | −1.77 | 165 |
| 10Y 2008–2019 | +0.207 | +0.97 | −0.233 | −1.06 | 210 |
| **10Y 2020–2026** | **+0.949** | **+3.39** | +0.137 | +0.44 | 116 |
| 30Y 1979–2007 | +0.385 | +0.80 | −0.241 | −0.63 | 78 |
| **30Y 2008–2019** | **+0.804** | **+3.86** | −0.203 | −0.94 | 160 |
| 30Y 2020–2026 | +0.432 | +1.41 | +0.453 | +1.52 | 91 |

The concession is a **post-GFC phenomenon**: weak everywhere pre-2008 (t ≈ 0.5–0.8), decisive in
2008–2019 for the 30Y (t = 3.86) and in the 2020+ **supply flood** for the 10Y (t = 3.39 — a
~4.7 bps cheapening per auction week). The **richening flipped sign after 2020** on both tenors
(+0.44 / +1.52) — post-auction bounce-back has vanished in the QT/supply-flood era. Sub-period
splits are descriptive era cuts declared up front (2008 = GFC/QE start, 2020 = pandemic
deficits), not snooped breakpoints.

## Third axis — do BIGGER auctions get bigger concessions?

Size is detrended (offering ÷ trailing median of the prior 8 same-tenor auctions — raw dollars
grew ~20×, an undetrended split would just compare eras), split at the median ratio; Welch t on
per-auction pre-window changes.

| tenor | big pre (cum) | small pre (cum) | Welch t (pre) | Welch t (post) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10Y | +1.55 bps (n = 308) | +1.88 bps (n = 180) | **−0.28** | −1.20 |
| 30Y | +2.25 bps (n = 244) | +0.90 bps (n = 77) | **+0.92** | −1.47 |

**BUSTED.** The dealer-balance-sheet story's own dose-response prediction — more supply, more
concession — fails: the 10Y points the *wrong way* (−0.28) and the 30Y points the right way but
nowhere near significance (+0.92). The concession is about the auction *cycle*, not the
relative size of the print.

## Tradability — long TLT over the post-auction window

Rule: enter at the auction-day close (calendar public weeks ahead; one lag exactly), hold 5
trading days, overlapping 10Y/30Y windows merge; cash earns bills; excess-vs-excess.

| leg | value |
|---|--:|
| TLT buy & hold excess of bills (beta yardstick, 100% exposure) | **+3.01%/yr** |
| Post-auction **alpha** (HAC reg on daily excess): ordinary day −0.80 bps/day, post-auction day **+5.19 bps/day extra** | t = **+2.26** |
| 2 bps/leg: 338 round trips, in-market 38.5% of days | gross **+4.25%/yr** → net **+3.69%/yr**, HAC t = **+2.11** |
| 5 bps/leg | net **+2.84%/yr**, HAC t = **+1.63** |
| per-trip gross | **+30.0 bps** vs 4 bps round-trip cost (2 bps/leg) |
| sub-period 2002–2019 (2 bps/leg) | net **+5.54%/yr**, HAC t = **+2.96** |
| sub-period 2020–2026 (2 bps/leg) | net **−1.32%/yr**, HAC t = **−0.33** |

At 2 bps/leg the round trip clears the bar on the full sample (net t = 2.11, and the
carry-clean alpha regression says post-auction days really were ~5 bps/day better than ordinary
days, t = 2.26) — but the edge **lived in 2002–2019 (t = 2.96) and is gone since 2020
(net −1.32%/yr)**, exactly where the yield-space richening flipped sign. Cost-sensitive
(t = 1.63 at 5 bps) and regime-dependent → **FRAGILE**, not INVESTABLE.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic yield random walk with synthetic auctions every 21 trading days; a planted
concession/richening V (4 bps in / 4 bps out per window) vs a zero-edge null. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamps.)*

| world | pre bps/day (HAC t) | post bps/day (HAC t) | fund trade net (t) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (0/0) | −0.051 (**−0.29**) | −0.173 (−1.04) | +0.21%/yr (+0.14) |
| planted 4/4 bps | +0.749 (**+4.25**) | −0.973 (**−5.82**) | +8.35%/yr (**+5.67**) |

The detector stays quiet on the null and lights up on the plant — the real-tape t-stats are
measurements, not construction artefacts.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED** (*Real on the cheapen-into leg · Weak on the richen-after leg*). Yields
  really do back up into 10Y/30Y auction days: **+1.55 bps** (10Y, HAC t = **+2.15**) and
  **+2.18 bps** (30Y, HAC t = **+3.27**) per auction week, strongest exactly where the supply
  story says (10Y post-2020 t = 3.39, 30Y 2008–2019 t = 3.86). But the second half of the
  claim — the post-auction richening — does **not** clear the bar in yield space (10Y t = −1.99,
  30Y t = −0.52) and flipped sign after 2020. No survivorship: official complete auction record,
  constant-maturity indices.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The post-auction TLT round trip is real on the full 2002–2026 tape
  at tight costs (net +3.69%/yr, HAC t = 2.11; carry-clean alpha t = 2.26) — but it is a
  2002–2019 phenomenon (t = 2.96) that has been **flat-to-negative since 2020** (net −1.32%/yr)
  and drops below the bar at 5 bps/leg (t = 1.63). Real but decayed/regime-dependent.
- **"Bigger auctions ⇒ bigger concession"? — BUSTED.** Size-detrended big vs small auctions:
  Welch t = **−0.28** (10Y, wrong sign) and **+0.92** (30Y, insignificant). The concession
  follows the auction *calendar*, not the size of the print — the dose-response half of the
  dealer story fails on 47 years of tape.
